what_was_established: Each callback is an `unsafe extern "C" fn()` taking no arguments, stored as EngineCleanupCb and registered by engine_table_register(Some(cb)) at two sites in its own file.

The engine lock is initialised before the callback can run: every path that reaches registration (ENGINE_new / ENGINE_by_id / ENGINE_get_first / ENGINE_get_last; RawEngine::new is private) runs the lock init, and GLOBAL_ENGINE_LOCK is stored once and never freed.

The lock is not held when the callback runs: engine_cleanup_cb_free's body (the registration/enqueue path reached only through engine_cleanup_add_first) invokes cb() without holding the engine lock, and the pinned authority's engine_cleanup_int (crypto/engine/eng_lib.c:175-184) runs that body while the lock is free. The discharge is conditional on engine_cleanup_int staying unlanded in the candidate: it does not exist in src/ at this identity, so no callback executes and the invocation-time lock state is authority-derived, not exercised. Landing it must re-open the nine sites and re-establish the precondition against the landed body.

The callback runs only after registration through that API; the callback body reads only its own module's `&'static EngineTableSlot`, so there is no caller-supplied pointer, extent, alignment or initialisation precondition.
The shared callee engine_table_cleanup takes the write lock itself; its initialised-lock precondition is documented at its `# Safety` (B20-TBL-3).
Sole invocation path is the withheld engine_cleanup_int; no call executes at afcfdc47e, so the invocation-path assumptions are derived from the pinned authority.
